# Colour of service businesses

## Problem statement

Service businesses render in a dark purple that is visually indistinguishable
from the flat purple face used by every upgrade card, so the two card families
read as the same thing at a glance on the street and in hand. At the same
time, an upgrade card carries no information about *what* it upgrades: all 39
upgrade cards share one uniform purple face regardless of the business they
apply to.

## Users

- **Main Street player** (primary) — scanning their hand and the market needs
  to distinguish a service business from an upgrade card instantly, and to see
  which family of business an upgrade belongs to without reading its title.
  - *As a player, I want service businesses in a colour no other card family
    uses, so I never mistake a service business for an upgrade card.*
  - *As a player, I want each upgrade card to show the colour of the business
    family it upgrades, so I can pick a relevant upgrade from my hand without
    reading every title.*

- **Colour-blind player** — the distinction must not rely on hue alone; the
  checkered pattern is itself a non-colour cue, and the upgrade card keeps its
  title and "for <Business>" target text.

## Existing state

- Synergy-type card faces are coloured from two parallel palettes:
  `CARD_FACE_PALETTE` (dark faces, `src/MainStreetCardsUtils.ts`) and the
  bright `synergyColor` accent palette. The static Node generator
  (`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) duplicates both; an
  existing test asserts the two copies of the face palette agree
  (MS-0MUZH51PU007POJ4).
- Service currently holds dark purple `#6A1B9A` (face) / `0x9B59B6` (accent).
- Upgrade cards are flat purple: background `#6B4C9A`, accent `#9B59B6`,
  rendered by `generateUpgradeCardSvg` / `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` and by
  `cardColorScheme` / the family branch in the `.mjs` generator.
- 39 upgrade rows in `src/card-data.csv` carry a `targetBusiness` name but no
  synergy column of their own; synergy must be resolved by looking the target
  name up among business **and** community-space rows (6 targets are community
  spaces: Community Garden, Health Kiosk, Library, Park, Playground, Town
  Fountain).
- 9 businesses are bridge cards with two synergy types; 11 upgrade rows target
  them (Cafe, Food Truck, Art Gallery, Day Spa, Flower Shop, Juice Bar, Yoga
  Studio, Teahouse).

## Desired change

1. **New service colour.** Replace Service's palette entries with a pink /
   magenta that no other synergy type uses, in **both** palettes (face and
   accent) and in **both** copies (TypeScript and the `.mjs` duplicate), so the
   palette-agreement test still passes.
2. **Checkered upgrade faces.** Upgrade card faces become a checkerboard of
   violet and the synergy colour of the business the upgrade targets, instead
   of the current flat purple.
3. **Bridge targets use both colours.** When the upgrade targets a card with

# Turn summary dialog suppressed by reduced motion setting

Discovered from: MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41 (End of Turn summary) / MS-0MVP46AMO002SZUT (dialog overlay).

## Problem

The Turn Summary dialog (MS-0MVP46AMO002SZUT) never appears for a player with the
reduced-motion setting enabled, even though the dialog itself is instant-appearance
(no fade, no tween) and therefore reduced-motion safe. The closing silently
auto-advances instead of pausing on the summary.

## Root Cause — two separate reduced-motion gates

1. **Display gate.** `shouldGateTurnSummary` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, ~line 544)
   returns `false` when `settingsPanel.reducedMotion === true`, so the dialog is never presented:

   ```ts
   if (s.replayMode === true) return false;
   if (s.settingsPanel?.reducedMotion === true) return false;   // <-- culprit
   ```

2. **Path gate (deeper).** Even if gate 1 is removed the dialog still cannot appear, because
   reduced motion never takes the deferred-closing path that the dialog gates. In `endTurn`
   (`MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, ~line 229):

   ```ts
   const deferred = !inTutorialBefore && !reducedMotion && !s.replayMode;
   ...
   result = processEndOfTurn(s.state, deferred ? { deferResourceApplication: true } : undefined);
   ```

   The engine only sets `requiresDeferredClosing: true` when `deferResourceApplication` is
   passed (`MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`, ~line 776). `shouldGateTurnSummary`'s first
   guard is `if (result.requiresDeferredClosing !== true) return false;`, so a reduced-motion
   closing has no deferred result and the gate is a no-op — the immediate path advances the
   day with no dialog. Removing only the display gate would therefore change nothing.

## Fix

Both need to change so that reduced motion is honoured by *animations* but not by the
*dialog*:

1. Remove the `reducedMotion === true` early return from `shouldGateTurnSummary`
   (keep replay / tutorial / competitive guards).
2. Let reduced motion take the deferred-closing path in `endTurn`, so
   `requiresDeferredClosing` is set and the gate has something to gate (keep tutorial and
   replay on their existing immediate paths). The reduced-motion animator already finalizes
   its income/incident presentation without tweens, so the deferred closing completes
   promptly; `deferUntilIncomeCollected` stays bounded so the closing can never hang.

Design note: with reduced motion the phased income show still schedules its
`INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS` (2.2 s) phase slots before the collect step runs, so the summary may
appear up to ~2.2 s × number of non-empty phases later. Confirm that pacing is acceptable,
or skip the empty-phase time in reduced motion, so the dialog does not feel like a hang.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A reduced-motion single-player `endTurn` produces a result with
   `requiresDeferredClosing === true` and `shouldGateTurnSummary` returns `true`.
2. The Turn Summary dialog is presented for reduced-motion players, and `[ Next Turn ]`
   resumes the deferred closing exactly once (day advances, HUD shows post-delta values).
3. Existing guards still suppress the dialog for replay, tutorial and competitive closings.
4. The dialog stays instant-appearance (no fade/tween) and plays SFX via `safePlaySound`
   (mute respected); no new animation is introduced for reduced motion.
5. Unit tests cover the guard matrix (reduced motion on/off × replay × tutorial ×
   competitive) and the `endTurn` deferred-path selection under reduced motion; a browser
   test asserts the dialog appears after a reduced-motion end-of-turn.
6. Changed-scope test gate passes; the dev-push gate (full suite) passes before merge.

# Intake Brief — Staff impact (MS-0MW20VBSZ003A01O)

## Problem statement

The GDD's staff treatment is thin and out of step with the (partially) implemented game: `the-build-gdd.md` still describes staff as a three-tier hand-capacity purchase (Appendix D.4), while the actual game already carries 26 staff cards with a sprawling, ad-hoc set of effects (hand slots, action points, per-business buffs, street-wide discounts, peeks, free re-rolls) with no coherent model. As a result, neither designers nor players have a clear mental model of what staff *are* or how they are meant to create efficiency and profit. This work item redesigns the staff system in the GDD around **two clearly differentiated staff types** — staff assigned to a **business** and staff assigned to the **management company** (the player) — so the design is complete, teachable, and gives each staff member a unique purpose.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — needs a clear mental model of the two staff types so hiring choices are meaningful trade-offs (business-specialist vs company-wide boosts).
- **Main Street player (new/learning)** — needs the game and its documentation to explain *why* a staff member is assigned to a business versus the management company.
- **Game designer / balance owner** — needs a single authoritative staff design in the GDD covering roles, impacts, and expected gameplay outcomes.
- **Implementing developer** — needs the redesign codified in the GDD before further staff implementation work.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want to understand the difference between staff who work at a single business and staff who run my management company, so that I can plan a coherent hiring strategy.
- As a Main Street player, I want each staff member to have a unique, clearly stated benefit, so that hiring feels like a meaningful choice rather than a flat capacity upgrade.
- As a game designer, I want the GDD to describe the complete staff system — roles, impacts, and expected outcomes — so that balance and implementation work has an authoritative reference.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Two staff types defined.** The GDD contains a complete Staff System section that defines and visibly differentiates the two staff types:
   - **Business staff** — assigned to a single business; effects are scoped *only* to that business (profit/income, cost reduction, reputation, synergy enhancement).
   - **Management-company staff** — assigned to the management company (the player); effects are player/turn-scoped (hand slots, action points, economy/environment insight, incident mitigation, etc.).
   The differentiation (scope of effect, where they are assigned, how the player interacts with them) is explicit and consistent.

2. **Example roles and impacts per type.** The section lists example staff roles for **each** type, and every example role states a **unique** benefit and the concrete magnitude/direction of its impact (e.g. "+X coins/turn to its business", "+1 action/turn", "reveals the top incident card", "reduces incident coin damage by Y%"). No two roles share the same benefit.

3. **Expected gameplay outcomes.** The section explains the expected gameplay outcomes for each staff type — how business staff drive business-level efficiency/profit, how management-company staff widen what the player can do in a turn — so a reader can see the strategic trade-offs between the two types.

4. **Consistency across documentation.** The redesigned staff model is reflected consistently in the surrounding design docs (`card-catalog.md` staff family description, `core-rules-and-mechanics.md` action/hand mechanics, `specialization-skills.md` where relevant); contradictions with the two-type model are removed or reconciled.

5. **Actionable for implementation.** The GDD section is precise enough to drive downstream implementation work: it names the two types unambiguously, defines how a staff member's type is determined/assigned, and makes scope of effect testable.

6. **Validation.** The documentation change is reviewed for internal consistency (cross-references resolve, no stale statements describing staff only as hand-capacity tiers) and any documentation checks the repo provides pass.

7. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Documentation-first redesign.** The primary deliverable is the GDD (and closely related design docs); engine/code implementation is out of scope for this work item unless discovered as follow-ups.
- **Two staff types only.** The design must commit to exactly two types (business vs management-company) — not a spectrum or a third category.
- **Management company = the player.** Per producer clarification, "management company staff" are player-level staff; the novelty is *communicating* the two-type distinction, not inventing a new in-game entity.
- **Backwards compatibility / existing content.** The redesign must account for the existing 26 staff cards (e.g. current street-wide effects map to management-company staff, per-business effects map to business staff) so the design is a coherent evolution rather than an unrelated parallel system.
- **Keep existing documented mechanics intact** (per-seat hand capacity, relocation action cost, tier gating) unless the redesign explicitly supersedes them.
- **UK English** throughout.
- No CHANGELOG.md edits (managed by the release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` staff treatment is minimal — Appendix D.4 "Staff Cards" describes only three hand-capacity tiers (Assistant/Manager/Director) with ongoing costs and no specialization model.
- `docs/game/card-catalog.md` documents 26 staff cards across generic hand-capacity cards, Group F ability cards, 12 specialization applicants, business-specialist cards, and the Investor — each with a `handSlotsAdded`, optional ability fields, and `allowedBusinessTypes`.
- `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` documents a 16-skill catalog in four categories (Income Boost, Reputation Boost, Cost Reduction, Incident Mitigation) with per-business vs street-wide scoping notes.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` `StaffCard` interface carries `handSlotsAdded`, `specializationSkillIds`, `employedAtSlot`, `allowedBusinessTypes`, `reputationPerTurn`, `refreshCostDiscount`, `upgradeCostDiscount`, `purchaseCostDiscount`, `taxAuditRate`, `actionsPerTurn`, `peekOncePerTurn`, `freeMarketRerollPerTurn`, `marketRelevanceBias`.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` and `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` implement buff math and skill catalog/assignment.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` documents action budget (staff `actionsPerTurn`), per-seat hand capacity, hire/relocate action costs.
- No single document currently frames staff as a two-type system — the distinction exists implicitly in the code (`employedAtSlot` vs hand-slot staff) but is not communicated as a design concept.

## Desired change

Rewrite/extend the GDD (primarily `the-build-gdd.md`, with consistency edits to related design docs) so it presents a **complete staff system** built on two explicitly differentiated types:

- **Business staff** — assigned to a business; unique per-business effects (profit/income, cost, reputation, synergy).
- **Management-company staff** — assigned to the management company/player; unique turn-level effects (hand slots, action points, insight, incident mitigation).

The document should include example roles for each type with their unique impacts, and articulate the expected gameplay outcomes and strategic trade-offs. It should be precise enough to guide subsequent implementation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` — new/expanded complete Staff System section (supersedes/extends Appendix D.4); two-type model, example roles, gameplay outcomes.
- `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — reconcile the Staff Cards family description with the two-type model; map existing 26 cards to the types.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — align staff action/hand mechanics wording with the two-type model.
- `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` — align skill scoping (per-business vs street-wide) with the two staff types.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `StaffCard` interface (reference for existing fields; implementation follow-ups only).
- `src/card-data.csv` — staff rows (reference for existing cards; implementation follow-ups only).
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` / `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — existing buff/skill wiring (reference only).

## Related work

- `MS-0MVBF45CB00515B0` — Staff relationship diagram (completed).
- `MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0` — Some staff cards should add action points (completed).
- `MS-0MUYAEXBN008YC0J` — Executive should grant an action point (completed).
- `MS-0MTISBYLS009936W` — Add Investor staff members (completed).
- `MS-0MUOSUKUC004G2VO` / `MS-0MUOSUNYR0073SI1` — Staff movement + action-point relocation gating (completed).
- `MS-0MV8PX4DV003LTFP` — Per-seat hand-capacity binding (completed).
- `MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M` — IT Specialist / Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects (completed).
- `MS-0MV8LHN5U008B9JJ` — AI staff should not give players bonuses (completed).
- `MS-0MUYK5BEC007L61X` — Mermaid diagrams for card synergies/staff relationships (completed).
- Staff specialization epic `CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK` and related tasks (`CG-0MT4WXNR80090FXZ`, `CG-0MT4WXZPX0040SA4`) — specialization skills.
- Docs: `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (Appendix D.4), `docs/game/card-catalog.md` (§ Staff Cards), `docs/game/specialization-skills.md`, `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — scope creep:** a full redesign could balloon into engine reimplementation. *Mitigation:* this item is documentation-only; implementation work is captured as follow-up items.
- **Risk — inconsistency:** the GDD may contradict `card-catalog.md` / `specialization-skills.md`. *Mitigation:* AC4 requires reconciliation across docs.
- **Risk — over-specification:** the design could lock in numbers prematurely. *Mitigation:* use directional example magnitudes and flag balance for playtest.
- **Assumption:** "management company = the player" (producer-confirmed); no new in-game entity is introduced.
- **Assumption:** the existing 26 staff cards are remapped into the two types rather than discarded.
- **Assumption:** business staff effects stay strictly business-scoped; management-company staff effects stay strictly player/turn-scoped.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the GDD be updated to document the fully implemented staff system, or should it focus on a redesign with new concepts?" — Answer (producer): "1. redesign". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "The description mentions staff assigned to the management company (turn-wide boosts). Is this a new concept or the existing street-wide specialization skills? / Is 'management company' a separate entity?" — Answer (producer): "2. it is only a new concept in terms of communicating the concept of two types of staff. The management company is the player." Source: interactive reply.

# Engine DEVELOPER.md lists reduced motion among the paths that omit deferResourceApplication

Discovered from: MS-0MW20KSEG001DH1X (Turn summary dialog suppressed by reduced motion setting).

## Problem

`core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` (the Tableau-Card-Engine submodule), section *Deferred End-of-Turn Mutation* → bullet *Deferred `processEndOfTurn`*, says:

> Tutorial, reduced-motion and replay paths omit the flag (legacy immediate behaviour, no regression — AC5).

After MS-0MW20KSEG001DH1X the reduced-motion path does **not** omit the flag: the scene (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, `endTurn`) takes the deferred closing path under reduced motion, so the Turn Summary dialog has a `requiresDeferredClosing` result to gate on. Only the tutorial and replay paths still omit it.

## Why it was not fixed in the MS session

- `core` is a git submodule (a separate repository, detached HEAD at the engine pin `5a16c2f`). A working-tree edit leaves the submodule dirty, and `npm run build` runs `engine:sync` (non-soft), which **refuses** to sync a dirty submodule ("never clobber") — every later build in this repo would fail.
- A local commit inside the submodule is discarded by the next `engine:sync` (it checks out the remote target), so the fix would silently vanish.
- The engine checkout has no worklog (`wl` there reports "not initialized"), and pushing to the engine repo's `dev` is not authorised from a game-repo session.

## Fix

In the Tableau-Card-Engine repository, amend that bullet so only the tutorial and replay paths are named as flag-omitting, and state that the reduced-motion path takes the deferred closing so a game's Turn Summary gate can present its summary dialog (cross-reference the game-side behaviour).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` no longer claims the reduced-motion path omits `deferResourceApplication`.
2. The bullet names the tutorial and replay paths as the immediate/flag-omitting ones and explains why the reduced-motion path is deferred.
3. No code change is required; the engine's documentation guards (if any) still pass.

# Intake Brief — Gate specialization-skill effects by staff type (MS-0MW3LTMHT001PRDT)

## Problem statement

Specialization skills are assigned from a global 16-skill pool regardless of a staff card's type, and the street-wide folds aggregate every employed member's skills. As a result, a **business-staff** member can hold a **management-company-scope** skill (Cost Cutter, Negotiator, Brand Ambassador, the four incident-mitigation skills, the Town Gossip baseline) and leak a player/street-scope effect, while a **management-company** member can draw **business-scope** skills (Chef, DJ, Networker, …) that can never resolve. The shipped behaviour therefore contradicts the two-type model reconciled in `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` (and GDD D.4.8), where a skill takes effect only from a member whose type matches the skill's scope.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — needs specialization skills to be a meaningful, type-consistent hiring signal: a business-staff hire improves its business, a management-company hire improves the player's turn, never an unexplained cross-scope leak.
- **Game designer / balance owner** — needs the shipped behaviour to match the documented two-type model so balance tuning and the skill catalog are trustworthy.
- **Implementing developer** — needs a deterministic, testable gate that preserves seeded reproducibility and existing save compatibility.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want a skill held by a business-staff member to affect only that business, so that hiring decisions match the two-type model.
- As a game designer, I want assignment to draw skills consistent with a staff card's type, so that no card can hold an effect it can never realise.
- As a developer, I want the seeded assignment stream to stay deterministic, so that same seed ⇒ same game is preserved.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Scope gate (behavioural).** A business-staff member holding a management-company-scope skill (Cost Cutter, Negotiator, Brand Ambassador, any of the four incident-mitigation skills, or the Town Gossip baseline) produces **no** player- or street-scope effect; equally, a management-company member holding a business-scope skill produces **no** per-business buff. The Operations Manager salary discount remains a business-staff effect applied to its employing member.
2. **Type-consistent assignment (deterministic).** Business staff draw only business-scope skills; management-company staff draw only player-scope skills plus the Town Gossip baseline. The stacking caps (≤1 income-boost, ≤1 reputation-boost beyond baseline) remain per-member and type-neutral.
3. **Determinism preserved.** The assignment stream stays seeded and reproducible (same seed ⇒ same assignments); existing determinism tests continue to pass, and new determinism tests cover the type-consistent draw.
4. **Documentation updated.** `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` records that the follow-up gap is closed (or removes the follow-up section), and the GDD D.4.8 / `card-catalog.md` cross-references stay consistent. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. **Validation.** At least one automated test proves the scope gate (both leak directions) and the type-consistent assignment; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Preserve determinism.** The assignment RNG stays the dedicated `createSeededRng(numericSeed ^ 0x5eed)` stream; do not perturb the main RNG stream (deck shuffles, market draws, challenges).
- **Preserve save compatibility.** Skills persist as stable id arrays; the staff type is derived from `employedAtSlot` and must not require a new stored field.
- **No new skills or magnitude changes.** The 16-skill catalog and its magnitudes are unchanged; this item only gates effects and constrains assignment.
- **Two staff types only.** Business staff = has `employedAtSlot`; management-company staff = no `employedAtSlot` (GDD D.4.2/D.4.8). No third type or skill flag.
- **Documentation-only gap closure.** Update the follow-up section of `specialization-skills.md` to mark the gap closed; do not re-open the two-type design.
- **UK English** throughout.

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — `STAFF_SKILL_CATALOG` (16 skills, 4 categories); `assignSkillsToApplicant(rng)` draws from the **global** pool and always adds the Town Gossip baseline; `assignStaffApplicantSkills(state)` seeds assignments across the staff deck and market row. The catalog carries no scope/type field today.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — `getEmployedSpecializationSkills(state)` flattens **every** employed member's skills (street-wide); `getEmployedSpecializationSkillsForBusiness(state, slot)` flattens only that slot's members; `computePerBusinessSkillBuffs`, `computeIncidentSkillBuffs`, `computeStreetOngoingCostReductionPct`, `computeRefreshCostDiscount`, `computeStaffSalaryDiscount`, `computeReputationGainMultiplier`, etc. translate skills to effects.
- `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts`, `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`, `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — consume the street-wide and per-business aggregations.
- `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` — § *Shipped cross-type assignments — reconciliation follow-up* documents the two gaps and states they are not yet fixed; the skill table already classifies 8 business-staff and 8 management-company skills.
- Existing tests: `staff-skill-assignment.test.ts`, `staff-skill-assignment-state.test.ts` (determinism, stacking, baseline), `staff-skill-buff-wiring.test.ts`, `staff-effect-scoping.test.ts`, `specialization-skills-two-types.test.ts` (doc contract).

## Desired change

1. **Scope gate.** Make street-wide/player-scope effect folds read only management-company members' skills, and per-business folds read only business-scope skills from the employing business's members — so a skill is inert when its scope does not match its holder's type. Keep the Operations Manager salary discount as a business-staff effect.
2. **Type-consistent assignment.** Draw business-scope skills for business staff and player-scope skills for management-company staff, always keeping the Town Gossip baseline on management-company cards. Preserve the per-member stacking caps and the seeded, reproducible stream.
3. **Docs + tests.** Update the `specialization-skills.md` follow-up section (gap closed/removed) and GDD/card-catalog cross-references; add determinism and scope-gate tests.

- `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — skill scope classification + type-consistent `assignSkillsToApplicant` / `assignStaffApplicantSkills`.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — scope-gated `getEmployedSpecializationSkills` / `getEmployedSpecializationSkillsForBusiness`; per-business fold gating.
- `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts` — incident/reputation folds consume gated skills.
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — Negotiator refresh discount consumes gated skills.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` / `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — ongoing-cost and salary folds consume gated skills.
- `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` — follow-up section closed; cross-reference consistency.
- `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (D.4.8) / `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — cross-reference consistency.
- `tests/main-street/staff-skill-assignment.test.ts`, `staff-skill-assignment-state.test.ts`, `staff-effect-scoping.test.ts`, `staff-skill-buff-wiring.test.ts` — scope-gate and determinism coverage.

- **MS-0MW20VBSZ003A01O** — Staff impact (epic; completed). Parent of the documentation work that discovered this gap.

- Docs: `docs/game/specialization-skills.md`, `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (Appendix D.4), `docs/game/card-catalog.md` (§ Staff Cards).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — determinism regression:** changing the candidate pool per type alters the seeded stream; *mitigation:* dedicated tests assert same-seed reproducibility across both types, and the salt/main-stream separation is preserved.
- **Risk — partial gate:** gating only the assignment leaves a stale save or hand-built fixture with a cross-type skill leaking; *mitigation:* the scope gate is enforced at the aggregation site, not only at assignment, and tests cover a cross-type skill held by both staff types.
- **Risk — Operations Manager mis-scope:** it is a cost skill but a business-staff effect; *mitigation:* explicit AC/test that its salary discount applies only from the employing business's member.
- **Risk — scope creep:** temptation to re-tune magnitudes or rebuild the catalog; *mitigation:* catalog magnitudes are out of scope and unchanged.
- **Assumption:** staff type is derived from `employedAtSlot` (presence = business staff) and needs no persisted field.
- **Assumption:** the skill-scope classification is the one already recorded in `specialization-skills.md` (8 business / 8 management-company).
- **Assumption:** the existing determinism and doc-contract tests remain the acceptance baseline.

No clarifying questions were required: the seed context (work item description plus the reconciled `specialization-skills.md` follow-up section, GDD D.4.8, and the source code) fully determines the problem, scope, acceptance criteria, constraints, and key files. The discovering item MS-0MW2XMB0P002D95K already recorded the two gaps and the producer-approved two-type model, so the intake proceeds without an interview.

- Q: "Is the staff type persisted?" — Answer (derived): No. It is derived from `employedAtSlot` (business staff) vs no slot (management-company staff). Evidence: GDD D.4.2/D.4.8; `specialization-skills.md` § *Serialization & compatibility*.

**Headline:** `run_tests.py` cannot parse Vitest's default-reporter failure output, so a real browser-mode assertion failure is reported as `unparsed_failure` (gate `reason: unparsed`) and no `test-failure` work item is created — the operator is told the *command or configuration* is wrong when the *code* is at fault.

## Problem statement

The test runner's Node failure parser only understands TAP (`not ok N - <name>`) output, so a failing Vitest test yields **zero** structured failure records. This repo's Vitest projects (`npm test` for `unit`/`unit-cli`, and `npx vitest run --project browser …` for the serial browser suite) emit Vitest's default-reporter format: `FAIL  |browser (chromium)| <file> > <suite> > <test>`, a `× <test name>` tree marker, an `AssertionError`/cause line, and `Test Files 1 failed (1)` / `Tests 1 failed | 1 passed (2)` summary lines. None of those match the parser, so `failures == []`, the suite is classified `unparsed_failure`, and the finish gate reports `reason: unparsed` with an empty `Failures:` list instead of naming the failing test.

## Users

- **Implementing agent (primary).** As an agent finishing a work item, I need the test gate to name the failing browser test so triage can open a `[test-failure]` item and I can fix the code rather than hunt through a 40 s browser log tail.
  - `As the implement skill finishing MS-x, when a browser assertion fails I get reason: test_failure and a test name, not reason: unparsed.`
- **Operator/producer (secondary).** As the producer reading a red gate report, I need the reason to distinguish "fix the code" (`test_failure`) from "the command/configuration is broken" (`unparsed`), so I send the work to the right place.
  - `As the producer, a red browser run tells me which test failed and which file to inspect.`
- **Triage skill (downstream).** As triage, I need structured failure records (`test_name`, `stdout_excerpt`, `stack_trace`) so `check_or_create.py` can create or match the existing `test-failure` item instead of falling back to a `<suite exited 1>` placeholder.
  - `As triage, one failure record per failing Vitest test is enough to create the [test-failure] item with the real test name.`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A Vitest **browser-mode** failure output (default reporter: `FAIL  |browser (chromium)| <file> > <suite> > <test>`, `× <test name>`, assertion/cause lines, `Test Files … failed` summary) parses into at least one structured failure record whose `test_name` contains the failing file and test name, with a non-empty `stdout_excerpt` — pinned by a regression test built from the evidence in this item.
- [ ] The same parser handles the **unit/unit-cli** Vitest form (`FAIL  |unit| <file> > <suite> > <test>`) and the browser file-tree form, de-duplicates a test reported in both places, and never emits a record for the `Test Files …`/`Tests …` summary lines.
- [ ] With a parsed Vitest failure present, `run_suite` reports `failures` non-empty and **no** `notice_code` (`unparsed_failure`/`killed` not set), so the shared classifier (`gate_reason.py`) and `implement.py finish` report `reason: test_failure`; the end-to-end assertion is pinned by a test that runs a Vitest-shaped result through the gate classifier.
- [ ] Genuinely unparsable non-zero runs still classify as `unparsed_failure` (the existing Playwright/`ENOSPC` and inode-exhaustion fixtures keep their current classification), and TAP (`node --test`) and pytest parsing are unchanged.
- [ ] The audit skill's suite-failure path uses the same Vitest parser (it currently imports only `parse_node_failures`), so the audit does not report a `<suite exited 1>` placeholder for a Vitest assertion failure.
- [ ] The change ships with the regression tests above passing in the repo that owns the code, and all related documentation is updated (test-skill reference failure-parsing/notice sections, plus any statement that Vitest failures are unparsed).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Repository ownership.** The code lives in the shared skills repo (`SorraAgents`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`), not in this checkout — the same pattern as MS-0MVZJ3175002WZO2 (MS item, change committed on SorraAgents `dev`). # Loan payoff dialog: carry the payoff across a paused closing

discovered-from:MS-0MW3SN58E009HC84

## Goal (user story)

As a player whose loan retires in a turn that also pauses on an event-choice
dialog (or a bankruptcy bailout offer), I want to still see the debt-free
congratulation once the pause resolves, so that no payoff goes unnotified.

## Context

`MS-0MW3SN58E009HC84` presents the payoff dialog in the closing presentation
slot (`MainStreetLoanPayoffModel.presentLoanPayoffDialogs`), after the closing
animations and ahead of the End of Turn summary. Two pauses resolve **after**
that slot, so their payoffs are currently never presented:

- **Event choice**: `processEndOfTurn` retires the loan and then pauses
  (`choicePending`) before `finishTurnPresentation` reaches the presentation
  slot. The resume path (`onEventChoice` → `finishDeferredEndOfTurn`) builds a
  fresh result that does **not** carry `loanPayoffs`.
- **Bankruptcy bailout**: the deferred result pauses on the loan offer
  (`pendingLoanOffer`); `onLoanOfferChoice` resumes through
  `completeDeferredClosingTail`, which never presents payoffs. A declined offer
  ends the run, so game over correctly wins there; an **accepted** offer
  continues the run with no congratulation.

The paused path never duplicates a dialog (there is only one presentation slot),
so this is a *missed* notification, not a duplicate.

## Desired change

Carry the paused closing's `loanPayoffs` into the resumed flow (the same
pattern `pendingBankingHint` uses for the banking hint) and present them via
the existing `presentLoanPayoffDialogs` sequencer on the continuing resume
path — never on a resume that ends the run (game over wins).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An event-choice-paused closing that retired a loan presents exactly one
   congratulation when the choice resolves, and never two.
2. A bailout-paused closing where the seat accepts an offer (the run continues)
   presents exactly one congratulation; a declined offer (the run ends)
   presents the game-over overlay and no congratulation.
3. The dialog still appears only after the closing presentation and never
   alongside another modal.
4. Unit tests cover both pause paths, including the no-duplicate rule.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — carry the payoffs across
  `presentEventChoiceDialog` / `presentLoanOfferDialog` and present them on the
  continuing resume.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanPayoffModel.ts` — `presentLoanPayoffDialogs`
  (reused unchanged).
- `tests/main-street/loan-payoff-turn-flow.test.ts` — the pause/resume cases.

## Constraints

- Presentation only: no engine, arithmetic, wallet or RNG change.
- One modal at a time; the summary/bailout/event-choice pacing is unchanged.

# Enable bank loans in competitive play

Enable the human player's **mid-game bank loan** entry point in competitive
mode: the competitive Turn Summary panel's `[ Bank Loan ]` button, which is
today always disabled ("Bank loans are not available in competitive play
yet."), becomes interactive for the player's own seat, following the exact
single-player flow (option selector → take → re-render). The AI keeps its
bailout-only loan policy; bailout, repayment, HUD obligation and persistence
already work per-seat in competitive mode and are unchanged.

## Problem statement

The Bank Loans epic (MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG, shipped v0.1.23) delivered the loan
engine, per-seat competitive bailout, and the single-player End of Turn
summary entry point. The competitive Turn Summary panel (MS-0MVRNV9Y8008IKGK)
was deliberately shipped with `[ Bank Loan ]` **disabled** — a static
"not available in competitive play yet" hint — behind a per-seat-capable seam,
deferring per-seat mid-game loans. Today a competitive player can never choose
to take a loan during play, while an AI opponent hitting `coins < 0`
auto-accepts a bailout loan, so the player sees the AI borrow while their own
seat cannot — the asymmetry this item removes.

## Users

- **Human player, competitive mode** — "In competitive play I want the same
  Bank Loan affordance I have in single-player — the [ Bank Loan ] button on
  the Turn Summary, offered to my own seat when I am short of cash — so I can
  buy my way past a cash crunch exactly as an AI opponent does."
- **Producer / designer** — "Competitive loans must reuse the shipped engine
  and single-player UI patterns, not fork them; the AI bailout-only policy
  stays as decided (parent Q3 = A)."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Player-own-seat loan button.** In a competitive game (N ≥ 2) with
  `config.loansEnabled`, the Turn Summary panel's `[ Bank Loan ]` button is
  **enabled exactly when the human player's seat may borrow** (same rules as
  single-player: loans enabled, no active loan on that seat, a non-empty
  configured menu). Pressing it opens the existing mid-game loan selector
  driven by `config.loanOptions`; the disabled state otherwise shows a
  reason-specific hint (loans-disabled / active-loan obligation / no-options)
  instead of the static "not available in competitive play yet" copy.
- **AC2 — Per-seat correctness.** The loan taken from the competitive panel is
  booked to the **human seat** (explicit `ownerId` = the human seat id, via
  `findHumanSeatId`), never to the transient `activePlayerId` of a
  round-robin turn that may differ at the shared-day close; principal, log row
  and ledger credit match the single-player take exactly, and the loan is
  AP-neutral and undoable through the command surface (`takeLoanCommand` with
  the owner forwarded). A human seat already repaying a loan cannot take a
  second one (one-active-loan rule, unmodified).
- **AC3 — No regressions to shipped paths.** AI seats keep the bailout-only
  policy (no proactive AI lending — parent Q3 = A). The per-seat competitive
  bailout offer/accept/decline, standing repayment pass, HUD obligation
  readout (single-player + competitive scoreboard), loan payoff dialogs,
  save/load v3 round-trip and `loansEnabled: false` hard no-op all behave
  exactly as today, verified by the existing loan test inventory staying
  green.
- **AC4 — Testing/validation.** Tests cover: (a) the descriptor for the
  human seat drives the button's enabled/disabled state in the competitive
  panel, (b) an accepted take credits the human seat only and survives a
  re-render of the same `TurnResult`, (c) an active loan disables the button
  with the obligation hint, (d) `loansEnabled: false` / empty-menu keep it
  disabled, and (e) the mid-game take during a save/load round-trip.
- **AC5 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  change: `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (§5.1 two-entry-points
  paragraph currently states the competitive panel ships disabled "so per-seat
  mid-game loans arrive later"), in-game help copy where it mentions the
  Turn Summary `[ Bank Loan ]` button, code comments on the
  `COMPETITIVE_BANK_LOAN_HINT` / `showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog` seam, and
  any relevant docs-site entry (e.g. `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`).
- **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Reuse, don't fork** — the competitive panel keeps its per-seat model and
  single `[ Bank Loan ]` + `[ Next Turn ]` action row; enabling the button
  reuses the shipped `buildTurnSummaryLoanDescriptor(state, ownerId)`,
  `buildLoanSelectorModel`, `showLoanSelectorDialog` and `takeLoan`/command
  machinery rather than adding a parallel loan UI.
- **Human seat only** — the button is keyed to the human (player-controlled)
  seat; AI seats never get a proactive loan affordance (parent Q3 = A).
- **No engine-rule changes** — loan menu, interest, repayment, one-active-loan
  and shortfall semantics are untouched; this item wires an existing, already
  per-seat-capable path through the competitive presentation layer.
- **No action point and AP-neutral** — the take must not decrement
  `actionsRemaining`; the existing `takeLoan` no-AP rule already guarantees
  this and must not be loosened.
- **Non-blocking presentation** — a failing model build, an unbuildable
  descriptor/selector, or a scene without dialog support must never strand
  the shared day (existing gate contract).
- **Priority `critical` retained** — operator-set at dispatch; kept per the
  precedence rule even though the change is a net-new feature (classification
  would suggest `medium`/`high`) — flagged for producer re-confirmation.

## Existing state

- Engine is competitive-capable: `canTakeLoan`/`takeLoan` accept an `ownerId`
  and validate per seat (`src/MainStreetLoans.ts`), `creditLoanPrincipal`
  handles the `PlayerRecord` wallet plus the bound-seat `resourceBank` mirror
  (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`), and `resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures`
  offers the human seat a **pending** bailout (surfaced as
  `TurnResult.pendingLoanOffer`, resolved via `resolveCompetitiveLoanOffer`)
  while AI seats auto-accept the largest option inline.
- The competitive Turn Summary panel is built by `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary`
  (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`) and presented by
  `presentCompetitiveTurnSummaryGate` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`),
  which calls `showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog(summary, advanceOnce)` **without**
  `onBankLoanAction`.
- `showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`)
  renders `[ Bank Loan ]` always muted/inert with
  `COMPETITIVE_BANK_LOAN_HINT = 'Bank loans are not available in competitive
  play yet.'` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`) and ends with
  `void onBankLoanAction;` — the seam is accepted but intentionally unwired.
- Single-player reference flow: `presentTurnSummaryGate` builds a
  `loanDescriptor`, passes it to `showTurnSummaryDialog`, whose `[ Bank Loan ]`
  handler builds `buildLoanSelectorModel(s.state)`, opens `showLoanSelectorDialog`,
  `confirmSelection` runs `takeLoanCommand(state, optionIndex, { allowDuringClosing: true })`
  through the undo manager, and re-presents the summary from the same
  `TurnResult` (`MS-0MVXYCKFE000VF76`).
- `takeLoanCommand` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts`) currently forwards
  `ownerId = undefined` (the acting seat) to `takeLoan`; competitive takes must
  forward the human seat id instead (AC2).
- Docs: `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §5.1 "Two entry points" states
  the competitive panel ships disabled "until per-seat mid-game loans arrive";
  help copy in `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` already refers to the Turn
  Summary `[ Bank Loan ]` button (single-player framing).
- No loan work item is open on this gap (duplicate check performed — all prior
  bank-loan items are `completed`; this is the deferred competitive seam).

## Desired change

1. **Descriptor for the human seat.** In
   `presentCompetitiveTurnSummaryGate` (or the dialog seam), resolve the human
   seat id (`findHumanSeatId`) and build
   `buildTurnSummaryLoanDescriptor(state, humanSeatId)` (loans-disabled /
   active-loan / no-options / enabled) instead of the static hint; pass
   `onBankLoanAction` keyed to that seat into
   `showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn, onBankLoanAction)`.
2. **Enable the button in `showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog`.** Mirror the
   single-player button: interactive in normal colour when the descriptor says
   enabled, muted/inert with the descriptor's reason-specific hint otherwise;
   drop the `COMPETITIVE_BANK_LOAN_HINT` static copy (keep the exported
   constant or replace with descriptor-driven text). Wire the pointer handler
   to open the per-seat mid-game selector (via `buildLoanSelectorModel` /
   `showLoanSelectorDialog`) and re-present the same `TurnResult` panel after
   the take, exactly like the single-player panel (`returnToSummary` pattern).
3. **Per-seat take.** Ensure the take is booked to the human seat: extend
   `takeLoanCommand` to forward an `ownerId` (or add a per-seat variant)
   calling `takeLoan(state, optionIndex, humanSeatId, { allowDuringClosing: true })`,
   executed through the shared undo manager; the selector's confirm path in the
   competitive panel must pass the human seat id.
4. **Docs & copy refresh.** Update `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`
   §5.1 (competitive panel is now interactive for the player's seat), the
   in-game help text and any UX-doc mention; update code comments that state
   the competitive button is "deliberately never wired".

### Non-goals / out of scope

- Proactive (non-bailout) AI lending — parent Q3 = A decision stands.
- Per-seat loan buttons inside each panel row — the panel keeps its single
  action row; the button is the human seat's.
- Any change to loan menu, interest, repayment, one-active-loan, shortfall or
  bailout semantics.
- Score/reputation effects of loans (existing follow-up space, not this item).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — replace the static
  `COMPETITIVE_BANK_LOAN_HINT` ("…not available in competitive play yet.") with
  descriptor-driven copy (or keep the export for the disabled fallback);
  `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary` gains the human seat's loan state if the panel
  needs to render it.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` —
  `presentCompetitiveTurnSummaryGate`: resolve `findHumanSeatId`, build the
  descriptor, pass `onBankLoanAction(seatId)` into
  `showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog`; the handler opens the selector and
  re-presents the same closing.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` —
  `showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog`: enable/wire `[ Bank Loan ]` per the
  descriptor; reuse `buildLoanSelectorModel` + `showLoanSelectorDialog` +
  `takeLoanCommand` confirm path (single-player `returnToSummary` pattern);
  replace the always-disabled rendering and `void onBankLoanAction;`.
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `takeLoanCommand`: forward an `ownerId`
  (defaulting to the acting seat) so competitive takes book to the human seat.
- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` — unchanged (already per-seat); only verification.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanSelectorModel.ts` —
  `buildTurnSummaryLoanDescriptor(state, ownerId)` already accepts the seat;
  confirm the competitive gate passes the human seat id. Possibly unchanged.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — §5.1 "Two entry points": describe
  the competitive panel's now-interactive button for the player's seat.
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` — help copy: mention the competitive Turn
  Summary `[ Bank Loan ]` for the player's seat.
- `tests/main-street/` — **new/updated**: competitive panel descriptor-gated
  button tests, per-seat take + re-render test, active-loan disables, loans-off
  / empty-menu disabled states, save/load round-trip mid-game take; existing

## Related work

- **MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG — Bank Loans** (completed, shipped v0.1.23). Parent

  persistence v3, docs. Its Non-goals explicitly deferred the Turn Summary

- **MS-0MVXYCIU00053HL1 — Loan eligibility in the deferred-closing window**

  competitive Turn Summary gate is the same window.
- **MS-0MVXYCJVU000QBK1 / MS-0MVXYCKFE000VF76 — mid-game selector + re-render

- **MS-0MVRNW5JT0046QI3 — Competitive summary invariants** (completed).

# Turn summary as a management-company profit/loss statement (MS-0MW4XULA90002OEY)

> **Status: FINAL — producer confirmed Q1=A, Q2=A, Q3=A (2026-11-06).** The
> brief below reflects those decisions. See the Appendix for the recorded
> questions and answers.

## Seed (producer)

> The turn summary should be a profit/loss statement for the management
> company. Each player should be on a separate tab with the default being the
> player.

## Problem statement

The end-of-turn **Turn Summary** currently presents a flat, two-column set of
figures (income, expenses, incident, one-off, net, closing balances) for the
human seat in single-player, and a dense block of per-seat text rows in
competitive play. Neither reads like a financial statement, so a player cannot
quickly answer "did my management company make a profit this turn, and where
did the money go?". The summary should be re-laid-out as a **profit/loss
(P&L) statement for the management company**, with each player's company on its
own tab and the human player's tab selected by default.

## Users

- **Single-player player** — after each closing, wants a compact P&L for their
  management company: income, expenses, adjustments and the bottom-line
  profit/loss for the day.
- **Competitive player** — wants the same P&L and to switch between each
  seat's management company with a tab, defaulting to their own.

**User stories:**

- As a player, after the closing I see my management company's P&L for the day
  (income, expenses, adjustments and net profit/loss), so I can see whether the
  day was profitable.
- As a competitive player, I can select another player's tab to compare their
  management company's P&L with mine.
- As a player, when the dialog opens my own tab is selected first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The end-of-turn Turn Summary presents the selected player's management
  company as a **coins-only profit/loss statement**: an **Income** section
  (base / synergy / reputation / events) with a total, a **Less: Operating
  expenses** section (staff / community / business) with a total, **Incident**
  and **One-off** adjustments, and an emphasised **Net profit/loss** bottom
  line. The displayed lines reconcile to the committed ledger
  (`incomeTotal + expensesTotal + incident.coins + oneOff.coins == net.coins`).
- Each player has its own tab; the human ("You") tab is selected by default
  when the dialog opens, and selecting another player's tab switches the whole
  statement to that player's figures.
- One unified tabbed P&L replaces both the single-player
  `showTurnSummaryDialog` and competitive `showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog`
  layouts. Single-player shows a single non-interactive "You" tab. Every value
  shown today is preserved — either as a P&L line or in the supplementary
  context — and no `TurnResult` ledger field changes.
- Non-monetary figures (reputation/score change, closing balances and
  businesses owned) are shown as **supplementary context** outside the monetary
  P&L lines, not as P&L lines. The existing **[ Next Turn ]** / **[ Bank Loan ]**
  behaviour is unchanged, including re-rendering in place after a loan take
  while preserving the selected tab.
- The dialog keeps the existing overlay conventions (instant appearance /
  reduced-motion safe, `hudContainer` parenting, depths 199/200/201, dismissal
  via `s.overlayObjects`, `safePlaySound` for buttons), and tabs are operable
  by pointer and keyboard.
- At least one automated test per surfaced P&L line and tab behaviour (model
  tests for the P&L/tab projection; browser overlay tests for rendering, the
  default tab and tab switching); all related documentation is updated
  (`docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` Turn Summary sections); and the full project
  test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **Presentation-only.** Consume the committed `TurnResult.turnLedger`
  (single-player) and `TurnResult.playerRoundLedger` (competitive). Never
  mutate state or consume RNG; the checkpoint stays in `finalizeTurn`.
- **No new engine accounting data.** Build the P&L from the existing line
  items: income by phase (base / synergy / reputation / events), ongoing costs
  by category (staff / community / business), incident coin/rep delta, one-off
  coin/rep delta, net coin/rep/score change, closing balances and businesses
  owned. Any genuinely new accounting line item (cost of sales, depreciation,
  interest, cash-flow statement, balance sheet) is a scope change and must be
  raised separately.
- **Overlay conventions** (AGENTS.md UI best practices): `createOverlayBackground`
  + `createOverlayButton` from `@ui`; all elements parented into
  `s.hudContainer`; depths 199 / 200 / 201; everything pushed into
  `s.overlayObjects` for dismissal; instant appearance (reduced-motion safe);
  button SFX via `safePlaySound`.
- **Preserve the loan seam.** The single-player `buildTurnSummaryLoanDescriptor`
  and the competitive per-seat descriptor plus the in-place re-render after a
  take must keep working. **[ Next Turn ]** remains the only way to resume the
  deferred closing.
- **Copy** in UK English.

## Existing state

- Pure models: `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` —
  `buildTurnSummary(state, result)` (single-player, owner-keyed `owners` rows,
  renders `humanOwner` today) and `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary(state, result)`
  (competitive, one `rows` entry per non-eliminated seat).
- Overlay: `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` —
  `showTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn, loanDescriptor, onBankLoanAction,
  result)` renders a two-column panel; `showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog(...)`
  renders one multi-line row per seat. Both use `createOverlayBackground` /
  `createOverlayButton` and share the `[ Next Turn ]` / `[ Bank Loan ]`
  pattern.
- Gate: `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` —
  `shouldGateTurnSummary` / `presentTurnSummaryGate` (and the competitive gate)
  slot the dialogs into the closing tail.
- Data: `TurnLedger` / `OwnerRoundLedger` in `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`
  carry every figure the panels show today.
- Docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § "Turn Summary panel model",
  § "Turn Summary dialog and the closing gate" and § "Competitive Turn Summary
  panel".
- There is **no existing tab-strip component** in the scene UI (searched
  `src/scenes/*.ts`); the tab strip would be new.

## Desired change

1. **Pure projection.** Add a Phaser-free profit/loss projection (in
   `MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` or a small helper) that turns a selected player's
   ledger figures into ordered P&L lines — total income, total operating
   expenses, incident and one-off adjustments, net profit/loss — with the
   non-monetary figures kept as supplementary context. Provide the per-player
   tab model (id, label, colour, is-human, default).
2. **Unified tabbed overlay.** Replace both flat layouts with one tabbed P&L
   panel: a tab strip (one tab per player, human default) plus the statement
   body for the selected tab. Single-player renders a single non-interactive
   "You" tab. Reuse the existing labels, fixed order and signed formatting.
3. **State and re-render.** Track the selected tab and preserve it across the
   in-place re-render after a loan take.
4. **Tests and docs.** Model tests for the projection and tab selection,
   browser tests for rendering/default tab/switching, and updated
   `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` sections.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — pure P&L projection per player/tab
  (income/expenses/adjustments/net, supplementary figures, tab model).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — unified tabbed P&L layout used by
  `showTurnSummaryDialog` and `showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog`; tab strip,
  default tab, switch handling, loan re-render with preserved selection.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — only if the tabbed dialog
  needs per-owner rows threaded through the gate (likely unchanged).
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — the three Turn Summary sections.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/turn-summary-model.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive.browser.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/helpers/turn-summary-dialog.ts`.

## Related work

- `MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41` — End of Turn summary dialog (completed): origin of the
  current dialog and ledger.
- `MS-0MVP45KZV006TMUK` — end-of-turn `TurnLedger` (completed).
- `MS-0MVP45WBA001GAVY` — Turn Summary model (completed).
- `MS-0MVP46AMO002SZUT` — Turn Summary overlay + browser test (completed).
- `MS-0MVP46Q8X003419R` — gating the summary into `finishTurnPresentation`
  (completed).
- `MS-0MVRNV9Y8008IKGK` — Competitive summary rows end-to-end (completed).
- `MS-0MVRNVHJ50095N9Y` — per-seat expenses (completed).
- `MS-0MVRNW26W0070CP0` — per-seat net and closing balances (completed).
- `MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI` — competitive end-of-turn summary parent (completed).
- `MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV` — End of game stats (completed): turn-by-turn graphs on
  the Game Over overlay — a distinct screen, not a duplicate.
- `MS-0MVXYCICT0051LU7` / `MS-0MW4YUHOU00474HZ` — Turn Summary loan descriptor
  and button (completed); must keep working.
- Docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § "Turn Summary panel model",
  § "Turn Summary dialog and the closing gate", § "Competitive Turn Summary
  panel"; `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` and
  `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` for the "management company" terminology.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Confirmed:** "management company" is the player's own company, so the P&L
  is per player (one statement per tab), not an aggregate across players.
- **Confirmed:** the P&L is monetary (coins); reputation/score, closing
  balances and businesses owned are supplementary context.
- **Confirmed:** one unified tabbed P&L for both modes; human tab default;
  preserve the selected tab across the loan re-render.
- **Risk (competitive regression):** the competitive panel carries more
  per-seat figures than the single-player dialog; the unified layout must keep
  all of them (as P&L lines or supplementary context).
- **Risk (loan re-render):** re-presenting after a take must rebuild the
  statement for the currently selected player and not reset unexpectedly.
- **Risk (reduced motion / input):** tabs must be instant-appearance and
  keyboard/pointer operable, with sensible focus behaviour.
- **Scope-creep risk:** new accounting artefacts (cash-flow statement, balance
  sheet, cost-of-sales subtotals, depreciation/interest lines) are out of scope;
  record them as linked work items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 — Which dialog(s) become the tabbed P&L?

Should the tabbed profit/loss layout replace **both** the single-player
`showTurnSummaryDialog` and the competitive
`showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog` with one consistent tabbed statement
(single-player showing a single "You" tab), or only one of them?

- A — One unified tabbed P&L for both modes; single-player shows one "You" tab.
- B — Only the competitive panel gets tabs; the single-player panel is
  relaid-out as a P&L but keeps no tab strip.
- C — Only the single-player panel is relaid-out; competitive stays as-is.

**Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-06): A** — one unified tabbed P&L
across both modes, single-player showing a single "You" tab.

### Q2 — What belongs on the P&L statement?

A P&L is monetary. The dialog currently also shows reputation/score, closing
balances and businesses owned. Which structure and which figures?

- A — Conventional coins-only P&L: Income (base / synergy / reputation /
  events) with a total, Less: Operating expenses (staff / community / business)
  with a total, Incident and One-off adjustments, then an emphasised Net
  profit/loss. Reputation/score, closing balances and businesses owned shown as
  supplementary context (header/footer), not as P&L lines.
- B — Strict monetary P&L only: coins, with reputation/score and businesses
  owned dropped from this dialog entirely.
- C — Keep every current figure and just relabel/regroup the two columns as a
  P&L.

**Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-06): A** — conventional coins-only
P&L with non-monetary figures as supplementary context.

### Q3 — Tab behaviour, default and persistence?

Confirm the tab behaviour: default tab, interaction, and what happens when the
dialog re-renders after a **[ Bank Loan ]** take.

- A — Default to the human ("You") tab on open; tabs are interactive and switch
  the whole statement; preserve the selected tab when the dialog re-renders
  after a loan take; single-player shows a single non-interactive "You" tab.
- B — Default to the human tab and always reset to it on re-render.
- C — Hide the tab strip entirely in single-player; show it only in
  competitive.

**Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-06): A** — human default,
interactive tabs, preserve selection across loan re-renders, single
non-interactive "You" tab in single-player.

# Ship release build advances configs/engine-pin.json without the core gitlink, failing the AC3 pin-contract test on the merged tree

**Headline:** A dev→main release runs the consumer repo's `npm run build`, whose `engine:sync` advances `./core` **and** rewrites `configs/engine-pin.json`; the ship skill's `regenerate-version.js` restores the staged gitlink but leaves the pinned SHA staged, so the release commit ships a pin that disagrees with the committed `./core` pointer and the `engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` "release pin contract (AC3)" test fails on the merged tree, blocking every release at the full-suite gate.

## Problem statement

The derived-files step can commit two halves of one engine composition in opposite directions: it restores the submodule pointer to the commit `HEAD` records yet keeps the pin file the same build rewrote. Every release of a game repo with an engine pin therefore risks a pin/gitlink mismatch that no human review catches — the mismatch only surfaces as a red pin-contract test on the merged tree, after the merge, bump and regeneration commits are already made and just before the release aborts.

## Users

- **Release operator (maintainer)** — runs `/skill:ship release` and needs it to complete without hand-repairing a tree. User story: "As a release operator, I want the derived-files step to leave one coherent engine composition behind, so a release is never aborted by a pin-contract failure that the release process itself created."
- **Game developer (internal)** — relies on the pin as the record of the engine a release was built against. User story: "As a game developer, I want the shipped pin to name exactly the engine commit the release tree records, so I can reproduce a release from source without guessing which of the two artifacts is lying."
- **Framework maintainer** — owns the ship skill and needs the rule to stay generic. User story: "As the ship-skill maintainer, I want pin restoration to be derived from the gitlinks the step already restores, so no consumer repo has to declare its pin path."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Framework rule in place: the pin is restored with the gitlink.** After staging tracked modifications, the ship skill's `regenerate-version.js` restores, for every gitlink it restores, any staged tracked file whose `HEAD` content carries the recorded submodule SHA and whose staged content carries the advanced one — index entry and working-tree file both back at `HEAD`. Delivered by the framework item `SA-0MW6LOXBO0008706` (blocker); this item records that commit and the resulting behaviour.
- **AC2 — Regression test reproduces this exact scenario.** The framework fixture advances a real local-path submodule **and** rewrites/stages `configs/engine-pin.json` exactly as `engine:sync` does; the test asserts the derived-files commit contains only the genuinely derived file, the recorded gitlink is unchanged, and the pin equals the recorded gitlink — plus a counter-case proving a pin the release bumped deliberately is *not* reverted.
- **AC3 — Replay proof on the preserved merged tree.** Re-running the fixed derived-files step on the preserved merged tree of `release/dev-to-main-20261107153603` produces a commit (or no commit) in which `git ls-files -s core` equals the `sha` in `configs/engine-pin.json`, and a full-suite run on that tree passes — closing out the `engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` "release pin contract (AC3)" failure captured in `/tmp/release/release2.log`.
- **AC4 — Rule documented where the derived-files behaviour is described.** `SorraAgents/docs/dev/release-process.md` § "Derived Version File Regeneration", `skill/ship/SKILL.md` step 5 and this repo's `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` state that a build-rewritten pin is restored with the gitlink, replacing the current claim that gitlink exclusion alone "keeps pin/pointer invariants intact".
- **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**
- **AC6 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**

## Constraints

- **Repository boundary** — the rule and its regression tests live in the framework (`SorraAgents/skill/ship`, `SorraAgents/tests/node`); this item owns the reproduction, the replay verification and the documentation reconciliation in `tce-main-street`. No `skill/` edits from this checkout.
- **Never bump a pointer in the derived-files commit** — `SA-0MVO274QN006GXGQ`'s guarantee is preserved, not reversed.
- **Generic, no per-repo configuration** — no pin-path list, no new `package.json` schema; the rule derives from the gitlink SHA pair alone, and repos without submodules behave byte-for-byte as before.
- **Non-fatal, tracked-files-only semantics unchanged** — a failed build still logs its warning and exits 0; `dist/` droppings are never staged.
- **No product-side build change is required in this item** — `npm run build` keeps sync-and-re-pin (`CG-0MVO268500071BPI`); the release-tree coherence is the ship step's responsibility.

## Existing state

Observed during the v0.1.24 → v0.1.25 release attempt (`/skill:ship release`, 2026-11-07). All release gates passed (unmerged branches, audit readiness, critical items, worklog refs, producer review, final validation); the merge script built the merged tree, created the merge and derived-files commits, ran the full suite and **failed**:

```text
all: FAIL [full scope] [type full] [full lane]
  notice: suite exited 1 with no parsable failures: all
```

Cached result identified the single failing test:

```text
FAIL |unit| tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts > release pin contract (AC3)
     > matches the committed ./core submodule pointer being shipped with the pin
❯ tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts:415:22
Test Files  1 failed | 462 passed (463)
```

The release aborted **before** tagging/PR (no new tag; code-freeze marker cleared; no work items closed).

Reproduction is still on disk:

| Evidence | Value |
|---|---|
| Failed branch | `release/dev-to-main-20261107153603` (local, unpushed) |
| Derived-files commit | `d2b98f9e` — "Regenerate derived version files for v0.1.25", touching only `configs/engine-pin.json` |
| Pin in that commit | `cee7fe0e40fdba829ca67bb5c3da826df33474a7` |
| `core` gitlink in that commit | `f9d0c74a2fa727da48a2ef4fed1af21704fd5024` |
| Release log | `/tmp/release/release2.log` |
| `dev` composition (pin and gitlink agree) | `f9d0c74a…` in both |

Root cause on the merged tree:

- `npm run build` = `npm run engine:sync && tsc --noEmit && vite build`; `engine:sync` (`node ./core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs sync`) advances the submodule to the engine remote tip **and** writes the new SHA into `configs/engine-pin.json`, staging the pin with the gitlink ("pin travels with the gitlink").
- `regenerate-version.js` then correctly restores staged gitlinks (index mode `160000`) to their recorded entries via `unstageSubmodulePointers()`, but the regenerated pin is an ordinary tracked file, so `git add -u` keeps it.
- The failing test compares `git ls-files -s core` with the pin's `sha`, so the derived-files commit guarantees a red result whenever the build advanced the engine.

This is the direct successor defect to `MS-0MVN0G6VB000ZF57` (spurious gitlink bump, fixed by excluding gitlinks, `SA-0MVO274QN006GXGQ`): excluding the pointer without also restoring its pin creates the mismatch.

An in-repo precedent for the same seam exists: `implement.py`'s finish gate restores build-originated composition churn (pin *and* gitlink, checkout moved back) from a pre-build baseline (`SA-0MVZE164P0048306`). It is a precedent in shape, not reusable code — that gate discards *all* build output, while the derived-files step must keep the genuinely derived files.

## Desired change

1. In `regenerate-version.js`, capture each staged gitlink's `recorded (HEAD) → advanced (index)` SHA pair before restoring it.
2. After unstaging gitlinks, restore (index + working tree) every staged tracked file whose `HEAD` content carries the recorded SHA and whose staged content carries the advanced SHA — the pin file, generically.
3. Report the restored pin paths in the structured result (`regenerateDerivedFiles()`) and in `merge-dev-to-main.sh`'s regeneration log line.
4. Extend both test copies with the pin-rewriting fixture and the deliberate-pin counter-case.
5. Re-run the fixed step against the preserved merged tree and record the replay evidence (commit, pin, gitlink, suite result) on this item.
6. Reconcile the three documentation sites with the actual rule.

Sequencing: the framework item `SA-0MW6LOXBO0008706` is a hard blocker — the replay in step 5 cannot pass before its fix lands. Steps 5–6 are this item's own work and must not start earlier.

## Key Files

- `SorraAgents/skill/ship/scripts/release/regenerate-version.js` — gitlink SHA pairs, pin restore, structured result, JSDoc header.
- `SorraAgents/tests/node/test-regenerate-version.mjs` — authoritative regression tests (pin-rewriting fixture, deliberate-pin counter-case).
- `SorraAgents/skill/ship/tests/test_regenerate_version.mjs` — skill-local mirror of the same coverage.
- `SorraAgents/skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — regeneration log line names the restored paths.
- `SorraAgents/skill/ship/SKILL.md` — step 5 description of the derived-files commit.
- `SorraAgents/docs/dev/release-process.md` — § "Derived Version File Regeneration".
- `tce-main-street/docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — § "What the finish gate commits" / release notes describing pin/gitlink coherence.
- `tce-main-street/tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` — the failing contract test; unchanged expected here, but the replay must show it green.
- `tce-main-street/configs/engine-pin.json`, `core` — the two artifacts whose agreement is the contract.

## Related work

- `Ship release derived-files step must restore a build-rewritten submodule pin alongside the restored gitlink (SA-0MW6LOXBO0008706)` — **blocker**: the framework rule, its tests and the release-process documentation.
- `Release derived-files step commits a spurious core submodule bump, breaking the engine pin contract (MS-0MVN0G6VB000ZF57)` — completed; the direct predecessor (opposite direction) whose fix created this defect.
- `Ship release derived-files step must never stage submodule pointer changes (gitlink exclusion) (SA-0MVO274QN006GXGQ)` — completed; the generic gitlink exclusion this item must extend without reversing.
- `Auto-sync engine submodule on dev builds; pin release builds to committed engine version (MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED)` — completed; the `engine:sync` / `engine:verify` split and pin policy (`CG-0MVO268500071BPI`) that make the pin travel with the gitlink.
- `Bump core submodule for the Gym storyline demo unit test (MS-0MVKNRV6T0019KHJ)` — completed; the deliberate pin+gitlink bump discipline (`tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` passes when both move together).
- `SA-0MVZE164P0048306` (framework) — finish-gate build-originated churn restore: same seam, complementary policy.
- `Engine pin lags the core dev tip, so engine:verify throws PIN MISMATCH (MS-0MVN1OAG1005JWFX)` — completed; establishes that a lagging pin is normal state and makes `engine:verify` fail, which is why "prefer `build:release`" (option C) cannot be the rule.
- `Re-pin core gitlink and engine pin to fix-carrying tip (MS-0MVOCF76S003HTQE)` — completed; the deliberate, reviewable pin+gitlink bump this item must keep possible.
- `npm run dev soft-syncs the engine submodule (never blocks local engine work) (MS-0MVZJ3JLG0074ACP)` — completed; the soft/strict sync split whose strict `engine:sync` behaviour triggers the desync.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVOCF76S003HTQE** – Re-pin core gitlink and engine pin to fix-carrying tip (completed)
- **MS-0MVN1OAG1005JWFX** – Engine pin lags the core dev tip, so engine:verify throws PIN MISMATCH (completed)
- **MS-0MVZJ3JLG0074ACP** – npm run dev soft-syncs the engine submodule (never blocks local engine work) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: aborted, ac4, acceptance, add, advance (+176 more)
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — matched: ac1, ac3, ac4, acceptance, add (+151 more)
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+147 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: over-broad restore.** A tracked file that happens to mention the advanced SHA could be reverted. Mitigation: both halves are required (`HEAD` carries the recorded SHA, staged content carries the advanced one) and only files the build changed qualify; AC2's counter-case pins it.
- **Risk: abbreviated SHAs.** A pin storing a short SHA would not match a full-SHA comparison. Mitigation: match with a minimum prefix length (default 7) against the recorded and advanced SHAs; recorded as an assumption in the framework item.
- **Risk: release still red for another reason.** AC3 attributes the failure to the pin mismatch only because the cached run isolated that single test; the replay re-runs the full suite rather than the single file, so an unrelated red tree surfaces immediately.
- **Assumption:** the pin is a *tracked* file — untracked/gitignored pins remain out of scope, consistent with the step's tracked-files-only rule.
- **Assumption:** the release tree's working `./core` checkout legitimately stays ahead of the restored gitlink after the step (the suite accepts any descendant of the pin); only the *committed* artefacts must agree.
- **Risk: scope creep** — teaching the ship step to verify consumer pin contracts, to prefer `npm run build:release`, or to re-pin deliberately as part of a release, is out of scope; record as linked work items.

## Options considered and rejected

- **B — Declared pin path** (e.g. `package.json` → `"ship": { "pinFiles": [...] }`): explicit, but adds per-repo configuration plus a schema to a step that is deliberately consumer-agnostic, and silently does nothing for a repo that forgets to declare its pin.
- **C — Prefer `npm run build:release`** (`engine:verify`) when declared: the release build then never advances the composition, but `engine:verify` fails whenever the pin lags the tracked tip (the normal state at release time), and the non-fatal path would skip regeneration altogether — a repo that derives a version file at build time would ship a stale one.
- **D — Commit the pin and the gitlink together** when the build advanced both: coherent, but it reverses `SA-0MVO274QN006GXGQ` and lets a release ship an engine commit that nobody selected; a deliberate engine advance must stay a separate, reviewable commit.

Chosen: the content-identified restore (§ Desired change), which is the ship-side analogue of the finish gate's rule, needs no configuration and preserves both existing guarantees.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: "Which rule closes the pin/gitlink desync — ship-side content-identified restore (A), ship-side declared pin path (B), product-side `build:release` preference (C), or committing pin and gitlink together (D)?"** — Answer (rgardler, interactive): **A — ship-side, content-identified restore**, recommended option accepted (generic, no per-repo config, preserves the never-bump-pointer guarantee; ship-side analogue of the finish gate's `_exclude_build_originated_churn`). Source: intake round 1, interactive reply.
- **Q2: "Where do the framework fix and its regression test land?"** — Answer (rgardler, interactive): **A — a linked SorraAgents item owns the framework fix + tests as a blocker; this MS item owns the main-street reproduction, replay verification and documentation reconciliation**, mirroring the `MS-0MVN0G6VB000ZF57 → SA-0MVO274QN006GXGQ` precedent. Evidence: created `SA-0MW6LOXBO0008706`; registered `MS-0MW6KN7T1002UCCI` → depends-on → `SA-0MW6LOXBO0008706`. Source: intake round 1, interactive reply.
- **Q3: "How is AC3 ('a subsequent release passes the gate') verified without waiting for v0.1.25 to ship?"** — Answer (rgardler, interactive): **A — replay the preserved merged tree** (`release/dev-to-main-20261107153603`, evidence `/tmp/release/release2.log`) with the fixed step and assert pin == gitlink plus a green full suite. Research: the failed branch is still present locally and its derived-files commit `d2b98f9e` reproduces the mismatch (`cee7fe0e…` pin vs `f9d0c74a…` gitlink). Source: intake round 1, interactive reply.

## Impact

Release operators can now run a dev→main release without hand-repairing the merged tree, and developers can reproduce any release from source because the shipped engine pin always names the exact `./core` commit the release tree records.
